title: One polynomial per eigenvalue: the kernels of the cut-open torus at powers of two
claim: Pre-registered 2026-11-10, before the proof attempt. At n = 2^m, h = n/2, q = 2n, for b in GF(q)* let X_b be the operator F -> (k + 1) F(k + 1) + Omega_b(k) F(k) mod k^h on F[k]_(<h), Omega_b(k) = b + sum over i = 2..m of b^(2^i) k^(h - 2^(i-2)), whose kernel is ker(I + C_s(b^2)) (LINEAR-ROOTS-20261109-001A, Theorem 2); K(b) the Kloosterman sum of GF(q) with x = 0 included and k_b = (|K(b) - 1| - 1)/2. Found before registration, to be proved: (1) the shift F -> (k + 1) F(k + 1) mod k^h and every multiplication mod k^h are self-adjoint for <F, G> = sum over j < h of [k^j](F G), so X_b is self-adjoint and its kernel is the radical of B_b(F, G) = <X_b F, G>; (2) any two solutions F_1, F_2 of X_b F = 0 satisfy F_1(k) F_2(k + 1) = F_1(k + 1) F_2(k); (3) hence the solutions are exactly G r(Y), Y = k^2 + k, r in F[Y], deg(G r) < h, for one polynomial G = G_b, and dim ker X_b = ceil((h - deg G_b)/2). Computed exactly before registration: (3) with deg G_b = h - k_b for every b at sides 8 to 128, so that (3) and deg G_b = h - k_b give the geometric multiplicity |K(b)|/4. Target, to be proved or left open with the point where the argument stops stated: deg G_b <= h - k_b for every b (the geometric lower bound), and lower bounds on the Jordan chains giving the algebraic multiplicity K(b)(K(b) - 2)/8, which prove the collapse (LINEAR-ROOTS-20261109-001A, Theorem 1).
failure_conditions: A side 2^m and b in GF(2n)* at which X_b is not self-adjoint for <F, G>.
Two solutions F_1, F_2 with F_1(k) F_2(k + 1) != F_1(k + 1) F_2(k).
A side and b at which the solutions are not G r(Y) for one G, or deg G_b != h - k_b (computed false at 8 to 128; side 256 is the stress run).
remaining_obligations: the target: deg G_b <= h - k_b and the Jordan chains, or the stopping point
foundation_claim_scope: The square torus of rule-60 rings with equally spaced law-(12, 12) contacts, cut open by a ring of cuts each way (A30, A32, A37, A38); its walk over GF(2), at sides 2^m. The spectrum is a contact-level reading, so it does not depend on how the rings are declared (A45).
